uncited: **Subdivision:** Subdivide the image tile into sub-tiles of 32 pixels (8x4 grid).
**Batching:** Iterate through the splat batches in chunks of 32 splats.
**Geometric Intersection Test:** Each thread $i$ (corresponding to splat $i$) pulls the bounding box of its assigned splat.
**Bitmask Creation:** Threads share their intersection results using the ballot primitive.
**Culling:** Each thread iterates through the 32 splats in the batch.
Using the bitmask, it checks if the bit corresponding to the current splat index is set.
*   **Synchronization Stalls:** The method avoids block-wide synchronization fences of the original blend stage by using warp-level lock-step execution.
*   **Workload Imbalance:** Not all splats in a tile will overlap and contribute to a pixel.
This creates an uneven distribution of work among threads.
*   **Time Complexity:** Reduces the number of expensive Gaussian alpha evaluations and memory fetches for non-contributing splats.
